jobs.title: Drift Wood #20 · a year in
jobs.prompt: a four-panel comic strip laid out as a two-by-two grid on a half page, thin black panel borders (4 panels). Style: black and white comic strip panel, scratchy crow-quill pen and ballpoint ink on cardstock, harsh photocopy contrast, heavy black spotting, jagged uneven line weights, 1990s indie comix zine style, xerox grain, no color, no gray tones. Cast, drawn the same in every panel, ages exactly as given: WOOD — aged 18, gaunt boy drawn a head too tall, oversized thrift-store wool overcoat to the knee worn indoors, faded black tee, dark jeans, sneakers, a bristol pad clutched flat to his chest, chin up; CHLOE — aged 18, girl with a sharp intelligent face, smudged heavy black eyeliner, straight dark hair to the shoulders, oversized dark cardigan, a Discman on her belt with headphones around her neck, a folded-back paperback, reads while talking; GULLY — aged 19, stocky boy with a round face, backwards blue cap, faded green hoodie with his hands in the front pocket, muddy tan work boots, easy slouch; THE LUNCH LADY — heavyset woman in a white cafeteria smock and hairnet holding a steel ladle, unimpressed posture. Title of the strip: DRIFT WOOD. The strip: Senior year. The strip is a year old. It marks it by not marking it. Panel 1: a school cafeteria serving line, a lunch lady ladling corn without looking up, a taller gaunt teenage boy in the same oversized overcoat holding out a tray (in this panel: WOOD, THE LUNCH LADY). Lunch Lady says "Corn or peas.". Panel 2: close-up of a teenage boy opening his mouth to speak and then closing it, cafeteria (in this panel: WOOD). No dialogue in this panel. Panel 3: a teenage boy in an overcoat at a cafeteria counter saying one word (in this panel: WOOD). Wood says "Corn.". Panel 4: a long cafeteria table with three teenagers sitting together at one end all facing a wall of rainy windows, black and white, no words (in this panel: WOOD, CHLOE, GULLY). No dialogue in this panel. Lettering: every balloon and caption contains its complete text exactly as written, in clean hand-lettered comic capitals, large enough to read; size each balloon to fit its whole sentence and never cut a word at a balloon or panel edge; no words other than the ones given. Bottom right margin: tiny signature "A. Finch — Small Wood, OR" beside a tiny stylized gull, two strokes. Reference @chloe_17 is the model sheet for CHLOE: match that face, build, hair and clothes exactly. Reference @gully_17 is the model sheet for GULLY: match that face, build, hair and clothes exactly. Reference @wood_20 is the model sheet for WOOD: match that face, build, hair and clothes exactly. Match the attached references: @chloe_17 for the character the strip's Chloe at 17; @gully_17 for the character the strip's Gully at 17; @wood_20 for the character Wood at 20-23.
